findings.issue: Adoption bypasses the verdict-aware same-head rule: a chained run C at an unchanged head that chains from a same-diff throwaway run B also adopts a separate blocking standalone run S, so S's findings are superseded and closed if C does not re-derive them.
findings.consequence: No concrete gate bypass was constructed: pr-ready findings are recomputed from live inputs each run, and lens/FSM findings carry their own run IDs. A pr-ready-owned finding that is not deterministically re-derived could close with no code change.

findings.issue: Same-diff adoption keys only on base SHA and head SHA, so an earlier standalone run over that head with a different working-tree state or mutation view is adopted as the same review.
findings.consequence: A chained run could close findings from that other run's uncommitted or view-specific changes that it never re-examined. Code-read only, not reproduced.

verdict.reasoning: The diff intentionally adopts all authenticated pr-ready runs for the same target and exact base/head as a chained run. The proposed finding identifies no concrete finding type or gate that can actually disappear, and admits that live pr-ready checks are recomputed while lens/FSM findings remain tied to their own run IDs. Without evidence of a non-recomputed pr-ready-owned blocker or the supersession logic alleged, the claimed bypass is speculative rather than a verifiable defect in this diff.

The diff intentionally defines review identity as the authenticated target plus base..head SHAs. Nothing shown establishes that uncommitted working-tree state or a separate mutation view participates in a pr-ready run but is omitted from those fields. TargetKey also constrains adoption to the same target. The claimed mismatch is therefore speculative and not verifiable from the supplied evidence.
